args.name: Build a small weather shelter
args.function: Provide a learnable practical method to construct a small shelter offering actual protection from rain and cold, using suitable locally obtainable materials.
args.conditions: I am outdoors in mild spring weather near a visible dry-grass plant. Fallen branches and vines have also been seen nearby, but I have not tested their suitability. I currently own two berries and no building supplies. Other people live nearby; shelter construction must not require controlling them or occupying their positions.
args.inputs: Suitable materials, a reachable unoccupied site, and any necessary tools; exact requirements are unknown and should be specified by a feasible method.
args.costs: Unknown. Specify actual materials, work time, energy, prerequisites and any learning required.
args.effects: Only completed construction should create a real shelter with specified protection and capacity. Do not assume available materials are suitable or grant mastery, supplies, happiness, or completed progress merely for requesting it.

candidates.function: Build a small open raised rack of 2 wood supports and 3 crosspieces that holds separated whole food off the soil; load and unload it, inspect it, compare stored roots with a carried control, maintain or dismantle it.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds. prepare: x, y in reach, orientation; materials: exactly 5 own whole untreated wood units (first 2 supports); optional food and quantity, the proposed load. Round 1 inspects pieces and site, 1 energy; a shortfall is reported and nothing reserved. Then 3 assembly rounds, 1 energy each; prepare naming the rack resumes. load: rack, food (own stack), quantity (at most 4), controlQuantity kept carried as tracked control; 1 round, 0.5 per unit loaded. unload: 0.5 per unit. inspect (anyone) or compare (at least 5 paired rounds): 1 round, 0.5. maintain: replace (piece ids) and as many materials; 1 round, 1. dismantle (empty): 1. cancel: 0. Refusals cost nothing; an unworked round pauses free.
candidates.effects: A unit is a 0.04 x 0.99 m rod (branch). Supports lie 0.8 m apart on firm ground; crosspieces 0.08 m apart make a 0.8 x 0.2 m deck 0.08 m up, one layer of 4 units, rated twice the weakest crosspiece (37 kg each: wood strength/2, bend 0.02 half-span). Pieces become one rack; none stays loose. Loading splits the stack exactly (decay, harvest, origin kept) and lays the lot on the deck under the food water rules; rain wets it, and rain water dries off at their evaporation limit. The decay increment of whole roots there is x0.8 (declared model coefficient) only while the rack is complete and sound, the lot fits, no other material lies on it, there is no rain or standing water, it is outdoors with wind and 0.25 m clear of solids, and the lot is not wetter or warmer than its control (without one, its loading water); else x1. Compare: decay gained by lot and control, exposure, the share unequal temperature explains, verdict. Wear 0.0005 + 0.002 x (rain + wind) a round; a loose crosspiece stops the rate, a loose support drops the food. No reward, refund or food.

response.text: {"queries":[],"result_json":"{\"reviews\":[{\"actor\":\"kai\",\"decision\":\"develop\",\"ability\":null,\"reason\":\"Develop a general small-shelter construction operation in the current-conversation handoff. The supplied searches for shelter, construction, covering, weaving and binding found no equivalent. prepare-ventilated-food-storage makes an open food rack: its rain-wetted deck does not provide a sheltered occupant volume or cold protection. Reuse its applicable construction infrastructure, not its functional identity. Kai owns no building materials; visible branches and grass do not establish suitability, ownership or sufficient quantities, and the mentioned vines have no supplied exact reference. These are execution prerequisites, not grounds for rejecting development.\",\"specification\":\"Implement Construct and maintain a small weather shelter, parameterized by mode (inspect, build/resume, repair, dismantle, cancel), site coordinates/orientation, exact material item IDs and quantities, and project/shelter ID. It is learnable by any applicable actor. Initial executable recipe: a hand-lashed, low A-frame thatched shelter, internal footprint approximately 1.6 m by 0.8 m, ridge 0.6 m high, capacity one curled or reclining person whose collision geometry fits. It is not standing accommodation, a fire shelter or protection against severe weather. Construction must not move or control other people. Entry and exit are independently chosen physical movements through a clear entrance; occupancy and protection follow actual position, fit and capacity, not ownership or an automatic teleport.\\nMaterials: 20 sound, untreated rods approximately 0.99 m long and at least 0.04 m diameter, allocated as six A-frame legs in three frames spaced 0.8 m apart, two overlapping ridge rods, four overlapping base rails and eight overlapping intermediate thatch battens; at least 30 m of sound flexible vine or equivalent cord, allocated to measured joints and thatch ties. Require 0.26 cubic metres of suitable long dry thatching material measured at its installed 0.10 m thickness, including roof and rear/end covering, plus 0.10 cubic metres of dry bedding. Leave an unobstructed entrance at one end. Record actual mass, dimensions, moisture and provenance; world resource-unit counts must be derived from those properties, never assumed to equal these volumes or lengths. No cutting tool is needed for the initial recipe: reject unsuitable dimensions before assembly rather than conjuring cut pieces. Substitutions use the same geometric, strength, flexibility and coverage checks. No material conversion may increase mass or yield free surplus. Twisting, bending, binding and overlapping thatch are new mechanisms to implement within this operation, not assumed mastered primitives.\\nSite prerequisite: reachable, firm, drained ground with the complete footprint, entrance and working clearance unoccupied and free of intersecting solids. Inspect visible conditions without revealing hidden deposits or unseen hazards. Ground clearance and collision checks run again at placement. Do not reserve another person's position, erase vegetation or excavate implicitly. If physical clearing is necessary, stop with that specific unmet prerequisite. Require sufficient accessible owned or explicitly supplied materials; no automatic gathering, trade, consent or ownership transfer. Relevant known sources are forest-dry-grass-0 at (14.2,16.3), forest-branch-0 at (17.2,13.3), start-2-branches at (16.5,20.4), and canopy-41 at (11.4,19.2). They are candidates only. The observed grass stock of eight and branch stocks are not verified engineering quantities or promised supplies. No exact vine source is supplied. Kai's item-5-kai-55 consists of two berries and is not a building input.\\nReuse navigate for actual travel, gather for exposed loose source material, pickup for existing ground stacks, and probe for optional separate material trials. Respect their existing costs and limits: gather spends 2 energy per transferred resource unit and removes finite source stock; probe costs one round and 0.2 energy for observation, or 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual sample unit for a physical trial. Do not charge a second probe fee for an inspection already included in construction. Borrow and record the existing prepare-ventilated-food-storage code for exact inventory escrow, staged assembly, ownership/provenance, wear and dismantling where applicable. Add shelter geometry, joint validation, thatch coverage, bedding and exposure calculations; record reused handlers/revisions rather than describing them as reinvention.\\nWork: inspect site and supplied materials for one round and 1 energy; report measured deficits with no material reservation if unsuitable. On a valid build, escrow exact inputs exclusively to its project. Frame assembly takes four active rounds at 1 energy each; roof/end covering four rounds at 1 energy each; bedding and final geometry/tie/coverage inspection one round at 1 energy. Total ten active rounds and 10 energy, excluding learning, collection, travel and optional trials. Each round requires reach, free working access and energy available under ordinary exhaustion rules. The declared recipe must pass deterministic joint-strength, overlap and coverage checks in code before this work can complete. If material units lack required physical properties, add measurement/validation to the handoff and block execution with an explicit deficit rather than inventing suitability. Studying, development and review never supply materials or construction progress.\\nTrack stage, exact completed work, material allocations, joint state, moisture, coverage and energy already spent. Interruption or lack of energy pauses work without a free active round; resuming the same project rechecks access, missing materials and structural condition, then continues retained work. Waiting and global review time do not perform work. Cancel costs no work round: release unincorporated escrow once; incorporated materials remain in an unfinished physical structure until dismantled. Death pauses the project and applies ordinary ownership/death rules without creating refunds or transferring it to another actor. No energy, study time, gathered stock or destroyed material is refunded. Another independently acting actor may work only through ordinary authorization and their own learned capability, access, inputs and paid work; none is compelled to help.\\nOnly successful final inspection emits shelter_completed and activates occupied-space protection. Intermediate products are explicitly unfinished frames, partial covering or bedding, with no completed-shelter modifier. Failed inspections emit actual measured reasons, not success. The completed product consumes its incorporated rods, cord, grass and bedding as component inventory; these items cannot simultaneously remain loose or fund another project. This initial design is rated only for rain up to 5 mm/hour, wind up to 5 m/s, no snow load, no flooding and no falling-object load. Those are conservative model design limits, not observed weather or universal engineering guarantees. In those conditions, while coverage and joints remain sound, route intercepted rain to the ground outside the footprint, permit at most 20% of otherwise incident rain onto the covered occupant, and multiply wind-driven convective exposure there by 0.5. Dry bedding reduces ground-contact heat loss by 50%. Never generate heat or raise ambient temperature; metabolic heat and existing thermal simulation remain the sources. Wet bedding loses its insulation benefit. No modifier applies outside the covered volume, beyond capacity, through an uncovered gap, or to someone who does not fit. Heavy wind, flood, snow, saturation or structural failure suspend the relevant rating and run ordinary exposure and failure rules; no promise of dry warmth in arbitrary weather.\\nRun ongoing water balance, ordinary plant-material decay and structural wear on world ticks, including while the builder is absent: incoming precipitation equals runoff plus stored water plus leakage; evaporation is limited by stored water and ambient drying capacity. Persist component moisture. Add normalized joint/cover wear of 0.001 per world round, doubled while rain or wind is present; existing material decay still applies. At condition below 0.75, use measured gaps and wetness rather than the full design protection; failed load-bearing joints disable occupancy protection and create an observable collapse with recoverable components and ordinary collision/damage processing. Repair identifies defective components and consumes equivalent real replacements, one round and 1 energy per rod or metre of cord, or per 0.05 cubic metres of installed covering/bedding, rounding work up; removed material remains as explicitly degraded output. Revalidate before restoring the rating. Empty-shelter dismantling takes two rounds and 1 energy each; output only surviving component quantities with their actual moisture, decay, damage and origin. Occupied dismantling is blocked until occupants independently leave. No fresh-material refund or automatic maintenance. All prerequisites, state transitions, costs, exposure limits, conservation, failure and repair rules execute in code, not recurrent model review.\",\"learning\":4,\"experienceReview\":\"Four individual study rounds teach this operation, without construction progress or automatic mastery. Requests, registration, naming, queries, waiting for development and study completion earn no pleasure or satisfaction. Leave protected reward accounts, budgets, goals and permissions untouched. Through the existing experience system only, an actual recorded informative material test or failed structural inspection may qualify as verified information gain if it establishes a new personally applicable fact with evidence; repeat checks of the same fact do not. Actual shelter use may produce physical comfort only from measured reduced wetness or heat loss, capped at 10 total physical comfort across overlapping sources, with no benefit when already equally dry and thermally comfortable. Do not reduce basic nutrition requirements because of mood or shelter. If the established experience system supports event-linked affect, allow at most one short pleasure unit after a first personally useful completed build or successful repair, decaying to zero within five world rounds, with an 80-round cooldown shared across functionally equivalent shelter work. Modest satisfaction may be sustained only by actual useful maintenance or applicable shelter use: cap at one unit, add at most 0.04 per qualifying world round, decay by 0.002 per otherwise inactive round, and never stack equivalent shelters or count mere ownership. Familiar legitimate maintenance may qualify without novelty. These are bounded eligibility proposals for the existing experience pipeline, not direct grants or new reward accounts; where no authorized channel exists, emit the real events only and award nothing.\",\"visualReview\":\"Emit observable inspection, material-tested, work-stage, interruption, repair, completion, leakage, wear, collapse and dismantling events with actor, project/object ID, location, tick, actual inputs/outputs, stage/progress and outcome. Persist reusable visual metadata: shelter type, footprint, orientation, ridge height, entrance geometry, component materials/colors, covered-area fraction, frame/tie condition, moisture, bedding state, occupancy and protection-active flags. Show an incomplete frame or partial thatch during construction; only successful final validation may display a completed shelter. Show actual gaps, dripping, wet bedding and broken joints as state changes, without invented occupants or emotional effects. Inspection failure or missing materials displays the failure/shortfall and retained progress, never a successful roof or protection badge. Visuals disclose only observable geometry and condition, not hidden source stock or unperformed tests.\"}]}"}
